mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1100 units signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Positive returns do not follow HOUST crossing above 1100 in 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% indicates a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE below 4% does not correlate with positive 20-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: When both real estate investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between joint increases in RSAFS and HOUST and S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth does not precede positive 20-day returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3% may signal tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS above 3% does not precede negative 5-day returns (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between GDPC1 growth and low UNRATE with S&P 500 returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) but remaining positive may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as markets anticipate sustained growth.
failure_condition: GDPC1 slowing growth in late-cycle does not correlate with positive 20-day returns.
